premise: At 60, after 31 years as a hospital housekeeper, I paid off my $225,000 bungalow, but my sister-in-law—who moved in as my caregiver after a hip replacement—forged a transfer-on-death deed leaving the house to herself and sold it to a vacation-rental investor for $350,000 while I was in rehab, mailing me a $4,700 'caregiver stipend' check. I proved the deed's notary stamp belonged to a notary who had died two years earlier, voided the sale, and now run 'Threshold of Deceit Respite Care' from the reclaimed bungalow, where she scrubs guest towels in a smock that says 'Deeded Me Out' and every receipt prints her deed-fraud docket.
